answer: Divergent-Challenge Liveness Test: each identity must answer a fresh random challenge (e.g., sign a zephyr-seeded nonce with per-identity state updated each epoch). Clones share identical state, so a clone answering correctly reveals it as a duplicate; only one copy can claim the reward, and the rest are flagged. Attackers must maintain distinct umber state per identity, raising per-identity cost to a unique secret plus ongoing update work—defeating mass duplication across the trellis of registered agents.
